excerpt: Hitting a deer and swerving to avoid one fall under different coverages. How animal collisions work in Georgia and South Carolina.
keyTakeaways: Hitting an animal directly is covered by comprehensive insurance if you carry it, while swerving into another object falls under collision coverage. Livestock owners who negligently let animals run at large can be liable under O.C.G.A. § 4-3-3 (Georgia) and S.C. Code § 47-7-110 (South Carolina). Georgia allows 2 years for injury claims (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and South Carolina allows 3 years (S.C. Code § 15-3-530). Minimum liability-only insurance does not cover animal strike damage to your vehicle.

faqs.question: Does comprehensive insurance cover hitting a deer?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you carry comprehensive coverage. Directly striking an animal is typically a comprehensive claim, not collision. You will pay your comprehensive deductible; insurers usually treat the claim as not-at-fault, so it is less likely than an at-fault collision claim to raise your premium, though it can still affect claims-free discounts.

faqs.question: What happens if I swerve to avoid an animal and hit another car?
faqs.answer: If you swerve to avoid an animal and hit another vehicle or object, the damage falls under collision coverage, not comprehensive. You may be found partially at fault for the swerve, which could increase your insurance rates.

faqs.question: Can I sue a livestock owner if their animal caused my accident?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the owner was negligent. Georgia (O.C.G.A. § 4-3-3) and South Carolina (S.C. Code § 47-7-110) both make it unlawful for an owner to let livestock run at large. Neither state makes the owner automatically liable when an animal gets out: you must show the owner failed to use ordinary care in fencing and confining it, though in Georgia an animal loose on the road lets a jury infer negligence unless the owner proves that care.

faqs.question: Does liability-only insurance cover animal accident damage to my car?
faqs.answer: No. If you carry only the minimum liability insurance required by Georgia or South Carolina law, you have no coverage for damage to your own vehicle from an animal strike. Only comprehensive coverage protects against animal collision damage.

faqs.question: What should I do after hitting a deer in Georgia or South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Pull over safely, call 911, do not approach the animal, photograph the damage and scene, check for injuries, and file a comprehensive insurance claim promptly. A police report strengthens your claim. Georgia requires notifying police of any injury or apparent damage of $500 or more; South Carolina requires immediate notice of any injury.

faqs.question: When is deer strike season in Georgia and South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Deer-vehicle collisions peak during October through December — the deer mating season (rut). During this period, deer are more active and more likely to cross roadways, especially at dawn and dusk.
